text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a p99 respike on the inference pool under the new routing patch. Not steady, comes in waves at high concurrency (>8k reqs/min).
Maria: Can you paste the numbers? p95/p99?
Alex: p95 ~ 85ms, p99 jumps from 320ms -> 1.2s during bursts. Throughput steady tho.
Josh: Interesting — sounds like KV cache churn. Any eviction log entries?
Alex: Yes, eviction rate spikes correlate. Kernel switching also increases in the same windows. Profiling attached (snippet):
```
KV_evicts: 142/s
kernel_switcher: 46% samples
microbatch_wait: 12% samples
sched_lock: 8% samples
latency_tail: ~1.2s p99
```
Priya: @infra-bot can you confirm node-level CPU/GPU scheduling during these bursts?
infra-bot: Collected host metrics for the period. GPU utilization ~72%, CPU user ~65%, io-wait ~1.2%. No OOMs.
Maria: If GPU not saturated, likely cache miss amplification + kernel fallback. When KV evicts hot prefixes, we rehydrate and kernel path sometimes falls back to slower attention kernels.
Josh: That's the suspicion. Microbatch sizing heuristic might be expanding during bursts causing larger batch queueing then cache misses amplify per-token work.
Priya: Replayed traffic in staging with a synthetic 10k rps burst. Repro steps:
1) loadgen --qps 10000 --mix chat,gen
2) enable routing v2
3) collect perf profiles
Result: p99 ~1.1s, eviction_rate 130/s, observed fallback to generic-kernel at sequence lengths >512.
Alex: Key ask: can we tune microbatch ceiling and KV hysteresis to reduce evictions under short hotset throbbing? Maybe smaller max_mb when eviction_rate rising.
Maria: Agreed — propose change: if eviction_rate > 50/s and p99 > 300ms, cap microbatch_size to 8 and lower max_batch_window_ms to 12ms. Also add hysteresis timer 30s before raising again.
Josh: Also add kernel selection metric: prefer quantized-kernel when fallback_count > 10 in last 60s. That is cheaper to rehydrate.
Priya: We should validate impact on throughput. In staging with cap_mb=8 throughput dropped ~9% but p99 improved from 1.1s -> 240ms.
Alex: That's promising. Any side-effects on cost (tokens/sec)?
Maria: Cost per token slightly up due to less batching, but overall SLO compliance improves. For critical customers we prefer latency. We'll make it rollout-gated.
Josh: Plan:
- PR: microbatch adaptive threshold + hysteresis (Maria)
- PR: kernel-selection guard (Josh)
- Run 4h canary on a subset of nodes (Priya)
- Monitor: p95/p99, eviction_rate, throughput, kernel_fallbacks
Priya: I'll prepare dashboard tiles and alert thresholds (p99>500ms -> rollback).
Alex: Sounds good. One more ask: add a lightweight flame sample of the kernel switcher stack on fallback to pinpoint hot functions.
Maria: Will include perfmap sampling every 10s for 2m after each spike.
Alex: Cool. If canary looks good, we can roll to remaining pool with 10% step increments and monitor for rollback triggers. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Canary job queued: job/evict-tune-canary-238765. Will post logs under /ci/canaries/evict-tune-238765.
Josh: Thanks all — I’ll spawn the PR for kernel guard.
Maria: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/patches/3245. Link in canary job.
Priya: Canary started. Will update with first 30m snapshot.
Alex: Thanks — keep thread updated.
